change_log.summary: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia expanded to more cities/energy sites; Yemen border restricted zone widened
change_log.detail: FCDO advice updated 20 Sep 2026: Houthi missile/drone attacks since mid-July 2026 now cited against Jizan, Najran and Yanbu (energy sites) in addition to Riyadh, Jeddah and Abha. The all-but-essential-travel zone along the Yemen border now explicitly includes the cities of Abha and Khamis Mushait in Aseer province.

change_log.summary: Jordan regional-tension record updated with specific 2024/2025 border-crossing attacks
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now cites a 2025 knife attack at the King Hussein/Allenby Bridge border crossing (3 deaths) and 2024 attacks on other border crossings that killed Israeli personnel, attributed to Iran-aligned militia groups.

change_log.summary: Added Niger Delta oil & gas offshore kidnap threat to Nigeria kidnap record
change_log.detail: FCDO advice specifically flags a high threat of kidnapping and armed attacks against Niger Delta oil and gas facilities, including offshore installations — this was previously not captured in the record despite being directly relevant to oil & gas personnel.

change_log.summary: La Guaira declared a military-controlled disaster zone after June 2026 earthquakes
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now notes earthquakes on 24 June 2026 (M7.2 and M7.5) led to La Guaira state — location of Venezuela's main international airport — being declared a disaster zone under military control with strict access restrictions.

change_log.summary: Added maritime attack risk and Israeli/Jewish-linked site targeting to UAE terrorism record
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now specifically flags increased maritime attack risk for vessels in the Gulf of Oman, Northern Arabian Sea, Gulf of Aden and Bab El Mandeb, and notes Israeli and Jewish-linked sites as potential targets given regional tensions.

change_log.summary: Added 23 new countries to the dataset (4 with sourced FCDO entry/security records, 19 with basic reference facts pending full records compilation)
change_log.detail: New countries with sourced records: Bahrain, Israel, Syria, Yemen. New countries with basic reference facts only (records not yet compiled): Argentina, Congo (Republic), Côte d'Ivoire, Cameroon, Colombia, Ecuador, Gabon, Ghana, Equatorial Guinea, Guyana, Mauritania, Peru, Sudan, Senegal, Suriname, South Sudan, Chad, Tunisia, Uganda. Also added 3 new operational locations for existing oil/gas countries: East-West Pipeline Corridor (Petroline) for Saudi Arabia, and Sharara Oilfield / Zawiya for Libya.

change_log.summary: Iran border-area restricted zone expanded to Sistan/Baluchistan and area east of Bam/Jask
change_log.detail: FCDO advice against travel now also explicitly covers Sistan and Baluchistan provinces and the area east of Bam and Jask (including Bam), citing banditry and drug-trafficking risk, naming Zahedan, Zabol and Mirjaveh as particularly insecure — in addition to the existing 100km Afghanistan-border and 10km Iraq-border zones.

change_log.summary: Israel–Lebanon (Hizballah) cessation of hostilities announced 16 April 2026
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now notes a cessation of hostilities between Israel and Lebanese Hizballah was announced on 16 April 2026, though fighting continues intermittently and hostilities could reignite with little warning. Movement-restriction advice for the Lebanon border area otherwise unchanged.

change_log.summary: Houthis formally designated US and UK as hostile states following February 2026 airstrikes
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now notes that following US/UK airstrikes in February 2026, the Houthis formally designated the US and UK as hostile states, escalating the threat level for the ongoing conflict.

change_log.summary: Bahrain has temporarily banned large public gatherings on roads/squares
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now notes the Bahraini government has temporarily banned large public gatherings on roads and in squares, in addition to existing general protest-disruption guidance.

change_log.summary: Oman terrorism record broadened to include places of worship/beaches/shopping centres and a July 2024 incident
change_log.detail: FCDO advice now lists a broader set of potential terrorism targets (adding beaches, shopping centres and places of worship to the existing list) and cites a July 2024 shooting near a mosque in Muscat that killed six people.

change_log.summary: Migrated TI data structure to the event/source-observation model
change_log.detail: Added events and sourceObservations collections and schema metadata. Existing countries, records, sources, locations, change_log and oilGasSummary were preserved. Existing records retain sourceId and are grandfathered; observations are required for new records going forward.

New event-based TI item (not a baseline record change): NATS reported a connectivity fault at its Prestwick control centre causing flight delays/cancellations across multiple UK airports on 21 Sep 2026. Single reporting chain (NATS's own statement, via The Connexion); published as REPORTED given non-sensitive, clearly-attributed operational content.
change_log.summary: Added Current Intelligence event: NATS technical fault disrupts UK flights (Prestwick, Scotland), 21 Sep 2026

change_log.detail: New event-based TI item: overnight drone attack on the Moscow region (20 Sep 2026) killed 3, struck the Moscow Oil Refinery, and prompted Rosaviatsia to impose temporary flight restrictions at four Moscow airports (400+ flights delayed). Two independent reporting chains (Reuters wire via The Moscow Times; Russian aviation/airport-operator reporting via Airways Magazine). Kept DRAFT pending human legal review given fatalities and an allegation attributing the attack to Ukraine sourced only to Russian officials.
change_log.summary: Added Current Intelligence event: large-scale drone attack on Moscow region, oil refinery struck, airport flight restrictions, 20 Sep 2026
Added Hurricane Polo flooding/landslide warning to Mexico (Guerrero, Michoacan, Oaxaca)
change_log.detail: FCDO's Mexico advice page was updated 22 Sep 2026 to add information about Hurricane Polo bringing heavy rainfall to the southwestern Pacific coast (Guerrero, Michoacan, Oaxaca), with a hurricane warning in place and risk of life-threatening flooding/landslides through the week of 21 Sep 2026. This was not previously represented in the Mexico ENVIRONMENT category, which had no existing records.

change_log.summary: Corroborated NATS Prestwick ATC fault event with independent CAA/airline reporting; updated impact figures
change_log.detail: Added a genuinely independent reporting chain (UK CAA statement plus Ryanair/easyJet/British Airways statements, via Aviation Today) to the 21 Sep 2026 NATS Prestwick connectivity fault event, distinct from NATS's own statement already on file. eventStatus raised REPORTED -> CORROBORATED. Cancellation figure updated to 227 flights (from the earlier midday estimate of 35 departures/37 arrivals).

change_log.summary: Confirmed Moscow oil refinery drone attack event with Ukraine's own official acknowledgement
change_log.detail: Added Ukraine's own official confirmation of the 20 Sep 2026 Moscow-region drone strike (President Zelensky and Ukraine's General Staff, via Kyiv Independent) plus refinery-side operational detail on the halt/restoration timeline (via Militarnyi). This resolves the prior gap that Ukraine had not commented in the sources on file. eventStatus raised CORROBORATED -> CONFIRMED. Kept in DRAFT; legalReviewStatus unchanged (REVIEW_RECOMMENDED) given fatalities and active-conflict attribution, pending human legal review before any public publication.

change_log.summary: New Current Intelligence event: Hurricane Polo (Category 4) affecting Mexico's Pacific coast
change_log.detail: Created a new PUBLISHED, CORROBORATED event for Hurricane Polo based on NHC's own public advisory #16 (24 Sep 2026) and independent CBS News reporting of Mexican state/municipal government response (evacuations, shelters, school closures) across Guerrero, Colima, Jalisco, Michoacán and Nayarit. Secondary reports of Pacific port closures could not be verified against a retrievable primary source and were excluded.

change_log.summary: Updated Hurricane Polo baseline warning record with FCDO's Baja California forecast timing
change_log.detail: FCDO's Mexico advice page was updated 24 Sep 2026 to add a forecast that Hurricane Polo will reach Baja California around 26-27 September, plus a recommendation to monitor the US National Hurricane Center and Mexican Meteorological Service. Updated record mx-environment-hurricanepolo accordingly with a new SourceObservation.

change_log.summary: Corrected UK national threat level record from unsourced 'low routine risk' to verified SEVERE
change_log.detail: The existing gb-security-general record described 'low routine risk' with no genuine primary source attached (notes field admitted it was an unsourced contextual summary). Verified against gov.uk's own official statement that JTAC raised the UK national terrorism threat level from SUBSTANTIAL to SEVERE on 30 April 2026, with no subsequent downgrade indicated. Updated the record and title accordingly and attached a real SourceObservation.

change_log.summary: Nigeria entry record refined with Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) screening detail
change_log.detail: FCDO's Nigeria entry-requirements page now specifically names Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) disease as the driver for enhanced screening/monitoring of air passengers from East and Central Africa. Updated ng-entry-yellowfever with this detail and a new SourceObservation.

change_log.summary: First Ecuador baseline records: 60-day state of emergency and FCDO advice zones
change_log.detail: Created first-ever TI baseline records for Ecuador, reflecting a genuinely current, FCDO-verified security situation (60-day state of emergency declared 15 Sep 2026, curfews in 4 provinces, advise-against-essential zones in 7 coastal provinces and the Colombia border zone) — not a historical backfill.

change_log.summary: Added Santa Marta heightened-security record following armed-groups operation
change_log.detail: FCDO's Colombia page was updated 23 Sep 2026 to note heightened security measures in Santa Marta after a major operation against armed groups, plus elevated risk along Route 90 (Troncal del Caribe). Added as a new location-specific record alongside the existing nationwide kidnap/crime and terrorism/armed-groups records.

change_log.summary: Corrected overstated Indonesia 'advise against travel' record
change_log.detail: The existing id-security-noall record claimed FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Indonesia. Direct verification of FCDO's Indonesia advice and regional-risks pages found no such designation currently in force — only area-specific cautionary language. Record content corrected accordingly.

change_log.summary: Added Kazakhstan SIM/IMEI registration requirement (COMMUNICATIONS)
change_log.detail: FCDO's Kazakhstan entry-requirements page describes a mandatory IMEI verification step (imei.kz) for local SIM card use, not previously represented in TI. Added as a new COMMUNICATIONS record.

change_log.summary: Hurricane Polo re-intensified to Category 5; updated Current Intelligence event with revised NHC advisory, CBS News corroboration and a Cabo San Lucas small-vessel port closure
change_log.detail: NHC Advisory #20 (25 Sep 2026) shows Polo regained Category 5 strength (180 mph, 900 mb), forecast to approach Baja California Sur early next week and weaken toward Category 1 before landfall. CBS News independently corroborates. Added a third, distinct local reporting chain (Cabo Sun) for a Mexican Navy small-vessel port closure at Cabo San Lucas from 23 Sep 2026, flagged as single-source local confirmation. Baseline FCDO-sourced warning record (mx-environment-hurricanepolo) left unchanged as the FCDO page itself has not been updated since 24 Sep 2026.

change_log.summary: China flood Current Intelligence event (GDACS/GLOFAS) marked RESOLVED
change_log.detail: GDACS's own SEARCH API now returns iscurrent=false for this event with a final todate of 21 Sep 2026 and episode alert level downgraded Orange to Green; no new episode has been issued since. Moved from REPORTED to RESOLVED on that basis. Remained single-source/model-derived throughout its lifecycle and was never independently corroborated by TI.

records.title: High-standard but insurance/funds essential

records.content: Driving standards are poor with high accident rates. Traffic violations can result in vehicle impoundment plus fines. Desert driving requires proper equipment and a companion vehicle.

records.content: Zero tolerance applies to drugs (even trace amounts can mean 3+ months imprisonment or large fines). Public intoxication, swearing/rude gestures, and same-sex relations are all criminal offences that have led to arrest of British nationals.
records.title: Strict laws carry severe penalties

records.content: The UK government assesses a high threat of terrorist attack globally affecting British interests, including in the UAE. Potential targets include residential compounds, military and oil infrastructure, transport, crowded places, hotels and shopping centres. Ongoing regional tensions have increased the risk to Israeli and Jewish-linked sites, including in the context of maritime travel in the Gulf.
records.title: Terrorism risk affects the wider region including the UAE

records.content: Medical facilities are good but can be expensive, and public hospitals tend to be overcrowded.
records.title: Healthcare

records.content: Health risks include yellow fever, Zika and dengue; altitude sickness poses a risk in certain regions, and hantavirus is present in Argentina.
records.title: Disease risks

records.content: Pickpocketing and theft occur on public transport and at terminals, including a mustard-spray distraction scam; high-risk areas in Buenos Aires include La Boca, San Telmo Market, Palermo, Retiro and Florida Street. Armed robberies occur — victims should surrender valuables without resistance. Occasional 'express kidnappings' force victims to empty bank accounts.
records.title: Crime

records.content: Political demonstrations and picketing ('piqueteros') are more common than in the UK and can block major roads causing significant delays; avoid all protests and monitor local news.
records.title: Protests

records.content: There is a high threat of terrorist attack globally affecting UK interests; terrorist attacks in Argentina cannot be ruled out and could target foreign nationals indiscriminately.
records.title: Terrorism

records.content: 000 covers ambulance, fire and police services.
records.title: Single emergency number: 000

records.content: Strict quarantine rules apply. Travellers must complete an Incoming Passenger Card, declare biosecurity risk items (food, animal products, plant material, wooden items), and disclose farm/animal/wilderness contact within the past 30 days. Confiscation and fines apply for violations.
records.title: Strict biosecurity rules; declare food, animal, plant items

records.content: Passport must be valid for the length of planned stay; transit through other countries may require at least 6 months' remaining validity.
records.title: Passport valid for length of stay; 6 months for transit

records.content: British citizens must obtain an electronic visa: the eVisitor visa (651, free) or the Electronic Travel Authority (ETA, via app, free though service fees may apply). British-Australian dual nationals must enter/exit on their Australian passport.
records.title: Electronic visa required: eVisitor or ETA

records.content: Healthcare standards are very good. The UK-Australia Reciprocal Healthcare Agreement gives UK residents access to essential and urgent medical care; hospital emergency treatment is free, though GP visits and prescriptions carry charges. Non-reciprocal visitors may face substantial costs.
records.title: Very good; reciprocal agreement covers essential/urgent care

records.content: Health risks include dengue, Japanese encephalitis, and other insect- or tick-borne diseases.
records.title: Dengue, Japanese encephalitis, insect/tick-borne disease

records.content: Vast distances between towns demand careful planning; unsurfaced roads present hazards. Carry water, GPS and spare tyres, and inform others of travel plans on remote routes.
records.title: Vast distances; unsurfaced remote roads

records.content: Bushfire risk exists year-round, peaking November-February. Tropical cyclones affect Queensland, NT and WA November-April. Flooding follows heavy rainfall and cyclones; follow 'stay-at-home' or 'leave-now' orders immediately. Extreme heatwaves pose health risks throughout the continent.
records.title: Bushfires, cyclones and flooding by season/region

records.content: There is a high threat of terrorist attack globally affecting UK interests and British nationals, and terrorists are likely to attempt attacks in Australia. Recent incidents include a December 2025 antisemitic attack at Bondi Beach (15 deaths) and an April 2024 church incident in Wakeley, Sydney.
records.title: High global threat; recent attacks in Sydney/Bondi

records.content: Dangerous wildlife includes crocodiles, venomous snakes and spiders, sharks and jellyfish. Rip currents threaten swimmers.
records.title: Crocodiles, snakes, sharks and jellyfish

records.content: Ambulance emergency number: 103.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 103

records.content: Visitors need a passport valid for at least 6 months after arrival with 2 blank pages for stamps. Residents need at least 3 months' validity beyond their residence permit expiry.
records.title: Passport valid 6 months beyond arrival, 2 blank pages

records.content: Stays exceeding 15 days require online or in-person registration with the State Migration Service; failure incurs exit fines.
records.title: Stays over 15 days require registration

records.content: A visa is mandatory for all visits. Apply via the ASAN Visa e-visa service at least 3 days in advance; single-entry visas allow 30-day stays within a 90-day validity period. Business/work visas require contacting the Azerbaijani Embassy at least one month before travel.
records.title: E-visa mandatory; apply via ASAN Visa at least 3 days ahead

records.content: Medical facilities outside Baku are very limited. Even in the capital, serious illness or injury may require evacuation to Turkey or Western Europe. Carry a first aid kit for trips outside Baku.
records.notes: Relevant for any Caspian/offshore oil & gas site travel outside Baku.
records.title: Very limited outside Baku; evacuation may be needed

records.content: Altitude sickness is a risk in mountain areas including the Shahdag and Tufangdag ski resorts, Lake Batabat in Nakhchivan, and the Talysh mountains.
records.title: Altitude sickness in mountain resort areas

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel within 5km of the Armenia border due to landmine and unexploded ordnance risk from the 2020 and 2023 conflicts. Southwest regions affected by conflict carry similar risks.
records.title: No travel within 5km of the Armenia border

records.content: Baku has generally low crime, though bag-snatching and mugging occur, particularly after dark. Guard against card skimming at ATMs and during transactions.
records.title: Generally low crime in Baku; bag-snatching after dark

records.content: Illegal drugs (including cannabis) carry severe jail sentences and heavy fines. Drones are prohibited for non-residents without a special permit. Photography of military installations risks detention.
records.title: Drugs carry severe penalties; drone/photography restrictions

records.content: Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Azerbaijan, with potential targets including hotels, restaurants, energy sector facilities, religious sites, shopping centres, embassies and transport hubs.
records.notes: Fast-changing — review at least quarterly. Energy sector explicitly named as a target category — directly relevant to oil & gas travel.
records.title: Energy sector facilities identified as potential targets

records.content: Travellers involved in legal disputes, custody matters, or with unpaid debts may be subject to a travel ban that can become apparent only when attempting to leave the country.
records.title: Possible undisclosed exit/travel bans from legal or debt disputes

records.content: A visa is required; the standard tourist visa is issued automatically for two weeks (longer stays of up to six months are available), obtainable online in advance (e-visa), from the Bahraini Embassy in the UK, or on arrival. Passports must be valid for at least 6 months after the date of arrival.
records.title: Visa on arrival or e-visa available

records.content: Photographing security or military sites is prohibited and risks arrest and prosecution. Social media posts critical of the government or monarchy are treated as criminal activity. Public intoxication and drug possession carry severe penalties, including potential life sentences for trafficking, and disrespect toward Islam can result in a heavy fine or imprisonment.
records.title: Strict laws on photography, speech, alcohol and drugs

records.content: Protests and demonstrations occur regularly and can disrupt traffic and cause localised clashes between security forces and protesters; risk increases around anniversaries of significant events in Bahrain. Leave the area if a large public gathering or demonstration is seen.
records.title: Regular protests, risk rises around anniversaries

records.content: Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Bahrain, which could be indiscriminate and target places visited by foreigners including residential compounds, oil and transport infrastructure, restaurants, hotels, beaches, shopping centres and mosques — though no attack has been carried out successfully for several years.
records.title: Terrorism likely but no successful attack in recent years

records.content: Call 192 and ask for an ambulance.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 192

records.content: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date. Make sure the border control officer stamps your passport — if it isn't stamped, you may be fined on departure.
records.title: Passport valid 6+ months; ensure entry stamp is applied

records.content: British citizens can visit visa-free for up to 90 days for tourism. To extend, contact the Federal Police before the visa expires; overstaying incurs daily fines payable on departure or a later visit.
records.title: Visa-free for up to 90 days for tourism

records.content: Brazil poses disease risks including yellow fever, dengue, chikungunya and oropouche, alongside high UV exposure and altitude sickness in some regions.
records.title: Yellow fever, dengue, chikungunya and oropouche risk

records.content: Public hospitals in major cities are overcrowded with long waits and medication shortages, though foreign nationals do receive emergency treatment. Private hospitals require proof of financial capacity or insurance before admission.
records.title: Public hospitals overcrowded; private needs proof of funds/insurance

records.content: Robberies are common in many cities, particularly on buses, with mobile phones frequently targeted 4pm-9pm. Beach theft includes organised group robberies ('arrastões'). Express kidnapping — short abductions to force ATM withdrawals — also occurs.
records.title: Robbery, pickpocketing and express kidnapping in cities

records.content: The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to certain parts of Brazil — check the specific areas before travelling.
records.title: FCDO advises against all but essential travel to parts of Brazil

records.content: Favelas (informal urban neighbourhoods) pose unpredictable danger; tourists have been shot after accidentally entering favelas. Avoid favela tours and accommodation, and check that GPS navigation doesn't route through them.
records.title: Avoid favelas — unpredictable danger, including to tourists

records.content: Dial 911 and ask for an ambulance.
records.title: Emergency number: 911

records.content: Most short visits (typically up to 6 months) need an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) rather than a visa; this isn't required if arriving by land/sea with acceptable ID, or for dual British-Canadian nationals travelling on a valid Canadian passport.
records.title: eTA usually required instead of a visa for short visits

records.content: Your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay in Canada; many transit countries separately require at least 6 months' remaining validity.
records.title: Passport valid for duration of stay; 6 months for onward transit

records.content: Medical treatment can be very expensive with no special arrangements for British visitors; access emergency care via hospital emergency rooms or walk-in clinics.
records.title: Medical treatment can be very expensive for visitors

records.content: Cannabis is legal for recreational use within Canada, but it is illegal to take cannabis across the Canadian border without a permit or exemption — severe penalties apply.
records.title: Cannabis legal in Canada but illegal to cross the border with it

records.content: There is a threat of terrorist attacks in Canada; the FCDO assesses that terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks, which could be indiscriminate and affect places visited by foreign nationals. Past incidents include a 2023 stabbing attack in Surrey, British Columbia, and a 2021 vehicle attack in London, Ontario that killed four people.
records.title: Significant threat of terrorist attack

records.content: Western Canada faces a significant wildfire risk in summer — follow local warnings and news for the latest outbreaks. Winter storms (November-April) bring blizzards and freezing rain causing dangerous driving conditions. Tornadoes can occur May-September (peak June-July) in southern regions, hurricanes may affect coastal areas July-November, and avalanches are a risk in mountainous regions such as Alberta and British Columbia.
records.title: Wildfires common in western Canada in summer

records.content: Passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after arrival. A visa is mandatory: apply for an e-visa online at evisacam.cm (the service can have technical issues), or obtain a physical visa from a Cameroon embassy/high commission in advance — a visa on arrival is not available at Yaoundé or Douala airports, nor can an e-visa be obtained at land or sea borders.
records.title: E-visa or embassy visa required; no visa on arrival

records.content: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required to enter Cameroon.
records.title: Yellow fever certificate mandatory

records.content: Ambulance emergency number: 112.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 112

records.content: Medical facilities in Cameroon are below UK standards and emergency facilities are extremely limited; serious cases require medical evacuation to Europe.
records.title: Healthcare

records.content: There have been incidents of kidnapping and hostage-taking for ransom by large gangs across multiple regions; the UK does not make concessions to hostage takers.
records.title: Kidnap

records.content: Camouflage clothing is illegal, drug penalties are severe, photographing military/government sites is prohibited, and same-sex relationships are illegal. Security-force roadblocks are common; do not pay bribes.
records.title: Laws

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Cameroon and against all but essential travel to other parts.
records.title: Advice level

records.content: Following the October 2024 elections, protests and unrest can occur without warning, and tensions in the Anglophone regions could trigger violence affecting foreign interests.
records.title: Political unrest

records.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Cameroon. Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa operate primarily in the Far North Region, but attacks could occur anywhere including Yaoundé and Douala; improvised explosive devices are increasingly used, with attacks having occurred in Yaoundé.
records.title: Terrorism

records.content: Call 120 and ask for an ambulance.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 120

records.content: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date and have 2 blank pages for visas and stamps.
records.title: Passport valid 6+ months, 2 blank pages

records.content: Register your residence with local police authorities within 24 hours of arrival, and expect biometric data (fingerprints, photos) to be collected on entry.
records.title: Register residence with local authorities within 24 hours

records.content: Until 31 December 2026, British citizens can enter China visa-free for stays up to 30 days for business, tourism, or family/friend visits. Longer stays, work, or study require a visa arranged in advance — a tourist/business visa does not permit working.
records.notes: Time-limited exemption — re-verify closer to end of 2026.
records.title: Visa-free for up to 30 days until 31 Dec 2026

records.content: Medical care in China is not subsidised for visitors and carries substantial costs. Comprehensive travel insurance covering healthcare, evacuation and repatriation is essential.
records.title: Medical care not subsidised for visitors — comprehensive insurance essential

records.content: Tap water is unsafe in China; consume only bottled water. Notable disease risks include avian influenza and dengue fever (concentrated in Guangdong Province, mainly May-November).
records.title: Tap water is unsafe — drink bottled water only

records.content: China's broad national security laws mean foreigners may be detained without having intended to break the law, potentially for up to 6 months before formal charges. Exit bans can be imposed for commercial disputes or investigations, lasting months or years without notice.
records.title: Broad security laws create arbitrary detention risk

records.content: Drug possession carries severe penalties including lengthy imprisonment or the death penalty; random drug testing occurs at borders and in public spaces.
records.title: Severe penalties for drug offences, including death penalty

records.content: Terrorist attacks in China cannot be ruled out, particularly in places frequented by foreigners during national holidays and at transport hubs.
records.title: Attacks cannot be ruled out, especially around holidays

records.content: Up to 10,000 US dollars-worth of any currency can be brought into Colombia without declaration; amounts above this must be declared to customs. A yellow fever certificate is required if arriving from a transmission-risk country and may be requested for travel to high-risk areas within Colombia.
records.title: Declare currency over US$10,000; yellow fever certificate may be required

records.content: Passport should have an expiry date at least 6 months after the planned departure date. Visitors can stay up to 90 days without a visa for business or tourism, at the discretion of the immigration officer, and must show an onward or return ticket. The optional 'Check-Mig' pre-arrival registration can be completed via Migración Colombia between 72 and 1 hours before travel. British-Colombian dual nationals must enter and leave using their Colombian passport and Cedula.
records.title: Visa-free for 90 days; optional Check-Mig pre-registration

records.content: Ambulance emergency number: 123.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 123

records.content: Medical standards vary significantly: private clinics in major cities offer quality care, but public health facilities and those in smaller cities are generally ill-equipped and poorly funded, and ambulance services in remote areas are unreliable. Tap water is safe to drink only in Bogotá.
records.title: Healthcare

records.content: Key health hazards include yellow fever, Zika, malaria, dengue and chikungunya. Altitude sickness can affect travellers in Bogotá and the departments of Cundinamarca, Boyacá, Nariño and Antioquia.
records.title: Disease risks

records.content: 'Express kidnappings' occur, where criminals force victims to withdraw cash from ATMs; kidnapping rates remain high and foreign nationals in the oil, mining and related sectors have been targeted. Street crime, drug-assisted robbery and dating-app-enabled targeting of lone travellers occur in Bogotá, Medellín and Cali.
records.title: Kidnap/crime

records.content: The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to parts of Colombia.
records.title: Advice level

records.content: Protests and demonstrations happen regularly throughout the country and often start at short notice; violence risk heightens around elections.
records.title: Protests

records.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Colombia. Despite the 2016 peace agreement with FARC, many armed groups remain active and have targeted transport hubs, markets, hotels, places of worship and public areas with little warning.
records.title: Terrorism/armed groups

records.content: Ambulance emergency numbers: 16 or 1021.
records.title: Ambulance emergency numbers: 16 or 1021

records.content: Cash exceeding €5,000 or equivalent must be declared at entry/exit; failure to declare is a criminal offence. Only residents may bring in Algerian dinars (max 10,000).
records.title: Cash over €5,000 must be declared

records.content: Passport must remain valid for at least 6 months beyond the arrival date. Invalid, lost or stolen documents will result in denial of entry.
records.title: Passport valid 6 months beyond arrival

records.content: A visa is mandatory for all visitors, obtained before travel via the Algerian Consulate in the UK (tourist visas may be available on arrival at certain southern airports with an approved local travel agency reservation). Overstaying risks detention, prosecution and up to 3 months' imprisonment.
records.title: Visa mandatory for all visitors; overstay risks prison

records.content: Private clinics offer better facilities than government hospitals; English is not widely spoken. Adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds for medical costs and repatriation are recommended.
records.title: Private clinics better than government hospitals

records.content: Altitude sickness is a notable risk in certain regions; consult TravelHealthPro for a full risk assessment.
records.title: Altitude sickness in certain regions

records.content: Algeria has a very high road traffic accident rate with erratic driving and minimal lane discipline; hazards include sand drifts, potholes and speed bumps.
records.title: Very high accident rate; sand drifts and potholes

records.content: A significant kidnap threat exists from groups such as AQIM and Daesh-affiliated organisations operating across North Africa; British nationals are considered legitimate targets. The UK government does not pay ransoms.
records.title: Significant kidnap threat from AQIM and Daesh-affiliated groups

records.content: Zero tolerance applies to drugs (penalties can include the death penalty). Public intoxication is illegal. Sexual acts between same-sex partners are illegal. Ramadan restrictions apply on eating, drinking and smoking in public.
records.title: Zero tolerance for drugs; same-sex relations illegal

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Algeria, particularly the southern border regions (kidnap concentration area), the Libyan and Tunisian borders, rural/mountainous areas north of Algiers, and the Sahara region.
records.notes: Fast-changing — review at least monthly. Relevant to any Sahara/desert oil & gas operations.
records.title: FCDO advises against all travel to southern border/Sahara areas

records.content: Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Algeria; attacks may target foreign nationals, including via lone actors. Recent incidents include IED attacks on soldiers in 2021.
records.title: High terrorism threat; attacks likely

records.content: Ambulance: 123. Fire: 180. Police: 122. Tourist police: 126.
records.title: Ambulance: 123, Police: 122, Tourist police: 126

records.content: Maximum 5,000 Egyptian pounds in/out; foreign currency over 10,000 USD must be declared. High-value electronics and recording equipment must be declared. Satellite phones/radio equipment are subject to confiscation without Ministry clearance.
records.notes: Satellite phone rule is operationally relevant for remote oil & gas site communications equipment.
records.title: Currency declaration rules; equipment restrictions

records.content: Passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after arrival and at least one blank page.
records.title: Passport valid 6 months beyond arrival, one blank page

records.content: British passport holders typically need a visa: online e-visa (valid up to 3 months), via the Egyptian Consulate, or on arrival at approved airports (30 USD cash, valid up to 30 days). No visa is required for under-15-day stays in Sharm El-Sheikh, Dahab, Nuweiba or Taba resorts if arriving by air. Digital visas at Cairo Airport from 1 Aug 2026 cost 36 USD by card.
records.title: Visa required; e-visa, on-arrival, or Sharm exemption available

records.content: Certain prescription and over-the-counter medications are controlled substances in Egypt and may require prior authorisation from Egypt's Ministry of Health. Travellers should carry a GP letter documenting condition, dosage and personal use, or risk confiscation and prosecution.
records.title: Some medicines controlled; prior authorisation may be needed

records.content: Some hotel doctors have significantly overcharged patients, though pharmacies outside hotels are more affordable. Specialised psychiatric care is limited outside major cities.
records.title: Hotel doctors may overcharge; specialist care limited

records.content: Health risks include dengue fever and tick-borne illnesses, particularly Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever; altitude sickness is a risk in certain regions.
records.title: Dengue and tick-borne illness including CCHF

records.content: Overall crime rates are low, but sexual assaults have been reported, particularly at Red Sea resorts, often involving accommodation staff. Female travellers should avoid solo taxi rides, especially at night.
records.title: Low overall crime; sexual assault reports at Red Sea resorts

records.content: Foreign nationals risk detention for political activity or government criticism, including social media posts. Drug possession carries life imprisonment or the death penalty. Photography requires permits near military/government sites; drones are prohibited without Ministry of Defence approval.
records.title: Political criticism risky; drug possession severe

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to certain regions and against all but essential travel to other parts — see the regional risks page for Sinai-specific detail.
records.title: FCDO advises against travel to parts of Sinai

records.content: Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Egypt, potentially targeting security forces, religious sites, public gatherings and foreign nationals. Recent incidents include a 2024 shooting in Alexandria and 2023 attacks on Israeli tourists.
records.title: Attacks likely; may target security forces and foreign nationals

records.content: General emergency number (ambulance, police, fire): 112.
records.title: Emergency number: 112

records.content: The EU's Entry/Exit System requires biometric registration (fingerprints and photo) on first entry to the Schengen area; free of charge and valid for three years.
records.title: EU Entry/Exit System (EES) biometric registration

records.content: Your passport must have been issued less than 10 years before your arrival date, and have an expiry date at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area. Passports renewed before 1 October 2018 may be affected.
records.notes: Stated for British nationals; verify equivalent rule for other nationalities.
records.title: Passport must meet Schengen age/validity rules

records.content: British citizens can enter visa-free for tourism, family visits, events or short study for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Time spent in other Schengen countries counts towards this limit; overstaying risks a 3-year Schengen ban.
records.title: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period

records.content: Public healthcare is generally adequate, but tourist areas may lack nearby public facilities, and private doctors/hospitals do not accept GHIC/EHIC cards. Travel insurance remains essential for repatriation and non-urgent treatment.
records.title: GHIC/EHIC does not replace travel insurance

records.content: Specific resort areas (Magaluf, Playa de Palma, San Antonio in Ibiza) see recurring dangerous balcony incidents and illegal commercial parties. There have been a number of serious accidents, some fatal, involving falls from height including balconies; travel insurance may not cover incidents involving alcohol or drug use.
records.title: Balcony falls and illegal parties in resort areas

records.content: The UK assesses a high threat of terrorist attack globally, and terrorists are considered likely to try to carry out attacks in Spain. Attacks can be indiscriminate, including in places visited by foreigners.
records.title: Terrorism threat assessed as high

records.content: Organised theft using distraction tactics is common, particularly at airports and around luggage handling. 'Highway pirates' target foreign-registered and hire vehicles; scammers may pose as plainclothes police to rob travellers.
records.title: Organised theft targets tourists, especially at airports

records.content: 999 (or the EU-standard 112) covers ambulance, fire and police services nationally.
records.title: Emergency number: 999 (or 112)

records.content: Most visitors to the UK need an ETA (Electronic Travel Authorisation) or a visa; requirement depends on nationality and purpose of visit. British and Irish passport holders, and those with permission to live/work/study in the UK, do not need an ETA. An ETA costs £20, is applied for online, and permits travel to the UK, Jersey, Guernsey or the Isle of Man for up to 6 months.
records.notes: Nationality-dependent — check gov.uk for the specific traveller's passport before booking.
records.title: Most visitors need an ETA or visa depending on nationality

records.content: A passport or travel document is required to enter the UK and should be valid for the whole of the stay (no fixed minimum extra-validity period is stated, unlike many other countries).
records.title: Passport must be valid for the whole stay

records.content: Nationalities that need a visa (rather than an ETA) can apply for a Standard Visitor visa, allowing tourism, family visits, business meetings and permitted paid engagements for up to 6 months. It costs £135 and can be applied for up to 3 months before travel. Paid or unpaid work (other than permitted engagements) is prohibited on this route.
records.notes: Relevant for non-ETA-eligible personnel (e.g. some Middle East/Africa passport holders) visiting UK offices.
records.title: Standard Visitor visa allows up to 6 months for business/tourism

records.content: Healthcare in the UK is of a high standard via the National Health Service (NHS). Emergency treatment is provided regardless of nationality, but visitors from countries without a reciprocal healthcare agreement with the UK may be charged for treatment, including hospital care.
records.title: NHS treatment; visitors from non-reciprocal countries may be charged

records.content: The UK's national terrorism threat level was raised by the Joint Terrorism Analysis Centre (JTAC) from SUBSTANTIAL to SEVERE on 30 April 2026 (an attack is 'highly likely'), following a stabbing attack in Golders Green, North London, and a broader rise in Islamist and extreme right-wing terrorist threat activity in the UK. As of the most recent official statement, the level has not been lowered since. Ordinary situational-awareness precautions remain appropriate, but travellers should be aware the threat level is elevated above routine.
records.notes: Previously an unsourced contextual summary claiming 'low routine risk'; corrected 24 Sep 2026 against JTAC/gov.uk's own primary statement, which shows the threat level has in fact been SEVERE since 30 Apr 2026.
records.title: National terrorism threat level: SEVERE (raised 30 Apr 2026)

records.content: All foreign currency must be declared on arrival, up to a maximum Ghanaian cedi equivalent of 10,000 US dollars; carrying more than this risks confiscation of the entire amount. Foreign nationals resident (or planning to be resident) for at least 90 days in a calendar year, aged 6+, must register with Ghana's National Identification Authority for a non-citizen Ghana card.
records.title: Currency

records.content: Passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date of arrival.
records.title: Passport valid at least 6 months after arrival

records.content: A visa is required. Apply online via the Ghana High Commission website; standard processing takes 10-15 days, with an express service (around 3 days) available at the Ghana Premium Application Centre in London. Yellow fever vaccination certificate required on arrival. Visa extensions are handled by the Ghana Immigration Service office on Independence Avenue, Accra.
records.title: Visa

records.content: Ambulance emergency number: 999 or 112 (ask for an ambulance).
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 999 or 112

records.content: Medical facilities are poor outside towns; adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds are essential, as serious cases require medical evacuation. Check vaccine recommendations, including for yellow fever, malaria and dengue, at least 8 weeks before travel via TravelHealthPro.
records.title: Healthcare

records.content: Robbery, burglary and serious assault have become more common since 2021, in some cases involving weapons. Street crime affects Accra, along with beach theft, airport luggage theft and vehicle attacks on specific high-risk roads. Criminally motivated kidnapping has occurred in Accra, Takoradi and Kumasi, targeting foreign nationals for financial or political gain; the UK does not make concessions to hostage takers.
records.title: Crime

records.content: Possession of even small amounts of cannabis can lead to a prison sentence of more than 5 years, usually after a long and expensive legal process, and bail is not normally granted. Some same-sex sexual acts could lead to a prison sentence of between 3 and 25 years. Photography near military installations and airports is prohibited.
records.title: Laws

records.content: The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to parts of Ghana (see the regional risks section for specifics).
records.title: Advice level

records.content: Terrorist attacks in Ghana cannot be ruled out and could be indiscriminate, including in places visited by foreign nationals such as northern border zones, beach resorts, hotels and places of worship. JNIM and Islamic State-linked groups are active in neighbouring Burkina Faso near the Ghanaian border.
records.title: Terrorism

records.content: Ambulance: 118. Fire: 112. Police: 110.
records.title: Ambulance: 118, Fire: 112, Police: 110

records.content: Complete the 'All Indonesia Declaration Form' online within 72 hours of arrival (free). Register with local police if staying in private accommodation (5 million rupiah fine otherwise). A Bali tourist levy of 150,000 rupiah applies on arrival in Bali.
records.title: Online arrival declaration and Bali tourist levy

records.content: Passport must be valid for at least 6 months after arrival and have at least 2 blank pages.
records.title: Passport valid 6 months beyond arrival, 2 blank pages

records.content: A visa is mandatory. Visa-on-arrival (500,000 IDR, 30 days, single entry) is available at major airports/seaports for tourism and some business; online visas can be applied for at least a week ahead with multiple-entry/60-day options, but must be approved before arrival. The 30-day visa can be extended once for a further 30 days within the initial period.
records.title: Visa mandatory; visa-on-arrival (30 days) or online e-visa options

records.content: Standards of local medical care can be poor and some tests cannot be performed reliably; psychological services are particularly limited. Remote areas lack capacity for serious injury/illness; good care can be prohibitively expensive.
records.title: Inconsistent standards; remote areas lack serious-injury capacity

records.content: Health risks include unhealthy air quality during dry-season wildfires (May-November), volcanic ash exposure, Zika virus, dengue fever, malaria, and rabies from street dogs and monkeys.
records.title: Air quality, Zika, dengue, malaria, rabies

records.content: Tap water is not safe to drink in Indonesia.
records.title: Tap water is not safe to drink

records.content: High rates of sexual assault are reported in Bali and Lombok; avoid poorly lit areas at night. Drink spiking incidents are documented in Bali, Lombok and the Gili Islands. Counterfeit alcohol containing methanol has caused deaths.
records.title: Sexual assault and drink-spiking reported in Bali/Lombok

records.content: All forms of cannabis are illegal with airports using advanced detection technology; drug possession carries lengthy prison sentences or the death penalty. Aceh Province enforces Sharia law, banning alcohol and prohibiting LGBT+ activity, gambling and extramarital relations.
records.title: Zero tolerance for drugs; Sharia law in Aceh

records.content: Volcanoes are active throughout Indonesia and can erupt without warning, with evacuation zones typically 3-7km. Earthquakes and tsunamis occur regularly. Flooding is common October-March; wildfires April-September generate widespread haze.
records.title: Active volcanoes, earthquakes and tsunamis

records.content: FCDO's Indonesia regional-risks guidance uses cautionary, warning-based language for specific areas (e.g. "the security situation in Highland Papua and Central Papua provinces is unpredictable and can change quickly") but does not currently designate any part of Indonesia as "advise against all travel" or "advise against all but essential travel." Travellers should still check FCDO's regional risks page for the latest area-specific cautions before travel to Papua, Central Sulawesi, Aceh or Maluku.
records.notes: Corrected 24 Sep 2026: the prior record incorrectly stated FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Indonesia. Direct verification of both the main advice page and the regional-risks page found no such designation currently in force.
records.title: No current FCDO 'advise against travel' zone in Indonesia; area-specific cautions apply

records.content: Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Indonesia. Islamist extremism remains elevated, with potential targets including beach resorts, hotels, markets, tourist attractions, embassies and airports. Heightened risk periods include Christmas, New Year, Easter, Chinese New Year, Ramadan and elections.
records.title: High threat; targets include resorts, hotels and airports

records.content: Since 1 January 2025, an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) is required before arrival, valid for 2 years and covering visits of up to 90 days; the ETA costs 25 new Israeli shekels and is applied for via the Israel Population and Immigration Authority. Passports must be valid for at least 90 days beyond the arrival date.
records.title: Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) required since Jan 2025

records.content: Entry may be refused to those who have publicly called for a boycott of Israel or Israeli settlements, belong to an organisation that has, or have publicly denied the Holocaust or the 7 October 2023 attack.
records.title: Grounds for entry refusal beyond standard requirements

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to Gaza and against all but essential travel to parts of Israel, including areas near the Lebanon border (affected by conflict with Hizballah) and near the Egypt border (kidnap risk).
records.title: Advises against travel to Gaza and parts of Israel

records.content: Rocket, drone and missile fire (including from Houthi forces in Yemen) poses a risk throughout Israel, including from interception debris; Ben Gurion Airport can face disruption. Two Houthi drones fell in Eilat in September 2025, injuring at least 20 people.
records.title: Rocket, drone and missile risk nationwide

records.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Israel and Palestine, with an increased threat of attacks including by individuals acting alone. Recent incidents include a September 2025 shooting in northern Jerusalem (six killed, eight wounded), bomb discoveries on Tel Aviv buses in February 2025, and multiple stabbing/ramming attacks.
records.title: Very likely terrorist attacks, including lone-actor risk

records.content: Emergency ambulance number: 122.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 122

records.content: Unless on a visit visa, travellers must undergo HIV and hepatitis testing within 10 days of arrival, repeated every 90 days.
records.title: HIV/hepatitis testing required for longer stays

records.content: Declare local currency exceeding 200,000 Iraqi dinars, or foreign currency/valuables over $10,000 USD equivalent.
records.title: Currency declaration thresholds

records.content: A visa is mandatory for all visits, applied for via the Government of Iraq e-visa portal at least 24 hours before travel ($160 USD, valid for a 60-day stay). A return or onward ticket is normally required. The Kurdistan Region has a separate e-visa/visa-on-arrival scheme valid only within that region.
records.title: E-visa required via Iraqi government portal (60-day stay)

records.content: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date and contain at least one blank page. Passports reported lost or stolen will result in entry denial.
records.notes: Relevant given ongoing placement at Eni LSC, Zubair.
records.title: Passport must be valid 6+ months, one blank page

records.content: Iraq presents health risks including Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever and malaria, plus respiratory risk from dust/sand storms and altitude sickness in some regions.
records.title: Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever and malaria present

records.content: Regular protests occur, sometimes with casualties. Curfews and vehicle bans may be imposed suddenly around holidays, pilgrimages or elections. Anti-British/American sentiment can escalate during political tensions.
records.title: Protests, curfews and vehicle bans can occur with little warning

records.content: There is a high threat of kidnapping throughout Iraq from terrorist and militant groups including Daesh. British nationals — including oil workers, business travellers and humanitarian workers — are considered legitimate targets. The UK government does not pay ransoms.
records.title: High threat of kidnapping nationwide

records.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Iraq, particularly in provinces with former Daesh strongholds (Anbar, Diyala, Ninewah, Salah Al-Din, Kirkuk). Attacks include bombings, rockets, mortars, shootings and vehicle-borne explosives, targeting airports, markets, hotels, government buildings and religious sites. Foreign nationals, including oil workers, are considered high-value targets. Drone and rocket strikes also target Coalition installations across Iraq, including in the Kurdistan Region, and Iranian targeting of Iranian-Kurdish opposition groups in the Kurdistan Region has increased during the recent conflict, with continued strikes near Rawanduz and Koya.
records.notes: Fast-changing — review at least quarterly. Directly relevant to Eni LSC placement.
records.title: Very high threat of terrorist attack nationwide

records.content: Dial 115 for an ambulance.
records.title: Emergency number: 115

records.content: A visa is mandatory (unless holding an Iranian passport), obtained either through an organised tour or with an in-country sponsor; the process is described as long and unpredictable, so apply well in advance. Passports with Israeli stamps may be denied entry, and Iran does not recognise dual nationality.
records.notes: The FCDO advises against all travel — see the SECURITY category.
records.title: Visa required via organised tour or in-country sponsor

records.content: Medical infrastructure varies considerably by location — urban centres offer reasonable facilities but remote areas have limited services, and there have been documented shortages of basic medicines nationwide.
records.title: Variable quality; shortages of basic medicines reported

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to Iran and warns British nationals face risk of arrest, detention and even a death sentence. The UK cannot guarantee evacuation or face-to-face consular assistance during a crisis.
records.notes: Fast-changing — review at least monthly. Directly relevant given regional oil & gas work.
records.title: FCDO advises against all travel to Iran

records.content: Travel within 100km of the Afghanistan border, or within 10km of the Iraq border, is strongly advised against. The FCDO page also lists the whole of Sistan and Baluchistan provinces, and the area east of Bam and Jask (banditry and drug-trafficking routes), as areas to avoid.
records.title: Avoid travel near the Afghanistan and Iraq borders and in Sistan and Baluchistan

records.content: Holding a British passport or perceived UK connections can be reason enough for detention. British-Iranian dual nationals may not be notified to the UK government if detained, and consular access is not guaranteed. Risk increases for anyone linked to civil society, journalism, or with connections to Israel or the US.
records.title: Very high risk of arrest/detention, especially for dual nationals

records.content: Terrorist attacks have occurred in Iran, including a January 2024 suicide bombing in Kerman that killed at least 84 people, and attacks at the Shah Cheragh mausoleum in 2022 and 2023 claimed by ISKP.
records.notes: Fast-changing — review at least quarterly. Added 2026-09-21 from a summarised read of the FCDO page; verify exact wording on the page.
records.title: Terrorist attacks have occurred, including mass-casualty bombings

records.content: Ambulance emergency number: 911.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 911

records.content: Your passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date you arrive in Jordan.
records.notes: Stated for British nationals; verify equivalent rule for other nationalities.
records.title: Passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond arrival

records.content: Visitors remaining over 14 days must register with local police within that timeframe, providing biometrics. Failure results in a 200 JOD fine on departure.
records.title: Stays over 14 days require police registration

records.content: A visa is mandatory. Options include a single-entry visa on arrival at airports/the Sheikh Hussein or North Border crossing (40 JOD, 3 months validity), or the Jordan Pass for tourism stays of 3+ nights (70-80 JOD, applied for online before arrival, includes tourist-site discounts). Non-tourism visits should apply in advance via the Ministry of Interior.
records.title: Visa on arrival, or Jordan Pass for tourism stays of 3+ nights

records.content: Medical facilities outside Amman and Aqaba are basic; in an emergency, seek treatment in Amman or Aqaba.
records.title: Medical facilities outside Amman and Aqaba are basic

records.content: There is a risk of escalating regional conflict; recent Iranian and US strikes have occurred in the region including near Aqaba. Avoid military/strategic facilities, follow local advice to shelter if instructed, and expect possible flight cancellations and airspace closures.
records.title: Risk of regional escalation, including strikes near Aqaba

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel within 3km of the border with Syria.
records.title: Avoid all travel within 3km of the Syria border

records.content: There is a high threat of terrorist attack globally affecting UK interests and British nationals. Iran-aligned militia groups have threatened US regional interests and are likely to continue carrying out attacks in Jordan; potential targets include hotels, shopping malls, restaurants, tourist sites and border crossings. Recent incidents: a 2025 knife attack at the King Hussein/Allenby bridge (2 deaths); three border-crossing attacks in 2024 (3 Israeli personnel killed); and in June 2026 one death and eight injuries at a World Cup public screening in downtown Amman.
records.notes: Fast-changing — review at least quarterly. Added 2026-09-21 from a summarised read of the FCDO page (page shown as updated 15 September 2026); verify exact wording on the page.
records.title: High terrorism threat; Iran-aligned militia attacks likely to continue

records.content: Dial 119 for an ambulance.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 119

records.content: Your passport must remain valid for the whole of your stay and have a blank page for the visa stamp. Passports reported lost or stolen will result in entry denial.
records.title: Passport must be valid for duration of stay, one blank page

records.content: British citizens can get a visa on arrival for tourism or business for up to 90 days without prior application; a further 90-day extension can be requested at a local immigration office. Work or study requires an appropriate visa arranged beforehand — overstaying can mean arrest, detention and a heavy fine.
records.title: Visa on arrival for tourism/business up to 90 days

records.content: Medical facilities are high standard, but treatment is expensive with patients responsible for full costs and insurance checks that may delay treatment.
records.title: High standard but expensive; full cost due upfront

records.content: Japan enforces strict anti-stimulant drug laws; some common items such as Vicks inhalers and certain allergy/cold medications or painkillers are banned. Foreign nationals have been detained and deported for bringing them in — verify medication legality with the Japanese Embassy in the UK beforehand.
records.title: Strict bans on common medicines (e.g. some inhalers, allergy/cold medicine)

records.content: Tokyo's entertainment districts (Kabukicho, Roppongi, Shibuya, Ikebukuro) carry a higher risk of crime at night. Victims of drink-spiking scams have reported large unauthorised credit card charges. Avoid touts who approach speaking English.
records.title: Drink-spiking and fraud in Tokyo entertainment districts

records.content: Japan is in a major earthquake zone with associated tsunami risk. Monitor local alerts and follow local authority instructions. Typhoon season runs June-December (peak July-September), bringing high tides, landslide and flood risk. Multiple active volcanoes require monitoring of local alerts.
records.title: Japan is in a major earthquake and tsunami zone

records.content: Travellers can be detained without charge for up to 23 days for minor offences. Drug possession carries zero tolerance with sentences of 6-17 years. You must carry your passport or residence card at all times.
records.title: Detention without charge possible; zero tolerance on drugs

records.content: Call 112 and ask for an ambulance.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 112

records.content: If your passport contains an Israeli stamp, you may be denied entry or a visa.
records.title: Israeli passport stamps may cause entry/visa refusal

records.content: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date; for residency visas, at least 2 years' validity is required.
records.title: Passport valid 6+ months (2 years for residency visas)

records.content: A visa is mandatory, available on arrival at Kuwaiti airports or online via the Ministry of Interior. British citizens born in Afghanistan, Iran, Iraq, Lebanon, Pakistan, Sudan, Syria or Yemen cannot get a visa on arrival and must apply through the Kuwaiti Embassy beforehand.
records.notes: Relevant given oil & gas travellers' varied birthplaces/travel histories.
records.title: Visa on arrival or online — exceptions for some birthplaces

records.content: Under Kuwaiti rules, visitors must obtain permission from the Kuwaiti authorities to carry certain prescription drugs before arrival — this covers many commonly prescribed medications, so prepare documentation well in advance.
records.title: Prior permission needed for certain prescription drugs

records.content: It is illegal and dangerous to go near Kuwait's borders with Iraq and Saudi Arabia without authorisation; armed patrols are routine and unexploded landmines remain present in some areas — avoid off-road driving. It is easy to miss the border posts between Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, so only use an authorised land border crossing.
records.title: Illegal and dangerous to approach Kuwait's borders without authorisation

records.content: There is a high threat of terrorist attack globally affecting British interests. Iran-aligned militia groups have threatened to target US interests across the region and have claimed attacks in Jordan and Iraq; US bases in Kuwait have also been hit by missile and drone fire. Potential targets include residential compounds, restaurants, hotels, beaches, shopping centres, mosques and oil/transport infrastructure.
records.title: High global terrorism threat; Iran-aligned militia activity in the region

records.content: Ambulance emergency number: 103 (operators may not speak English).
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 103

records.content: Cash declarations are required for amounts exceeding $10,000 USD on arrival; undeclared amounts may be confiscated with fines. Export is limited to $10,000 USD in foreign currency cash.
records.title: Cash declaration required over $10,000

records.content: Passport must be valid for at least 30 days from arrival with one blank page minimum. If holding a Kazakh visa, passport must expire at least 3 months after the visa's expiry.
records.title: Passport valid 30 days from arrival, one blank page

records.content: Accommodation providers or hosts must register a traveller's arrival with the authorities within 3 working days of entry.
records.title: Accommodation must register arrival within 3 working days

records.content: Visa-free entry for up to 30 days for business or tourism, with unlimited visits allowed, but cannot exceed 90 days without a visa in any rolling 180-day period. Longer stays, work or study require a visa/work permit.
records.title: Visa-free up to 30 days; max 90 days per 180-day period

records.content: Medical facilities are less advanced than UK standards and most staff do not speak English. Adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds for treatment or evacuation are essential.
records.title: Facilities less advanced than UK; insurance essential

records.content: Health risks include biting insects and ticks, and altitude sickness in mountainous regions.
records.title: Biting insects/ticks and altitude sickness

records.content: Robberies and violent theft occur mainly at night in expatriate areas (Atyrau, Aktau, Astana, Almaty) near nightclubs and bars. Pickpocketing is common in markets and on public transport. Drink spiking leading to assault has been reported.
records.notes: Atyrau and Aktau are the main Caspian oil-industry hub cities — directly relevant for oil & gas travel.
records.title: Robbery, pickpocketing and drink-spiking risk in cities

records.content: It is illegal to sell, distribute, import or produce e-cigarettes, vapes or e-liquid (up to 2 years' imprisonment). Disrespectful social media posts about religion, culture or national symbols are illegal. Drones require a licence. LGBT+ 'promotion' legislation introduced December 2025 risks fines, detention or deportation.
records.title: Vaping/e-cigarettes illegal; strict speech and LGBT+ laws

records.content: Gvardeyskiy village (Almaty region), Baikonur town, and Karmakchi and Kazalinsk districts (Kyzylorda region) are restricted without special permission.
records.title: Some areas require special permission

records.content: Terrorist attacks in Kazakhstan cannot be ruled out and could be indiscriminate, including in places visited by foreign nationals.
records.title: Terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out

records.content: Ambulance emergency number: 1415. Medical help in remote areas may not be available and rescue operations have uncertain status.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 1415

records.content: Libya is a cash-based society — bank cards cannot be used at banks, ATMs or hotels, and ATM access is severely restricted. Amounts over $10,000 USD must be declared. Exporting Libyan dinar is illegal; use only Central Bank-approved exchange offices.
records.notes: Operationally significant for any personnel travelling to Libya — arrange cash logistics before travel.
records.title: Cash-based society; bank cards largely unusable

records.content: Passport must be valid for the entire duration of stay. Passports showing previous travel to Israel will be rejected. Lost or stolen passports result in entry denial.
records.title: Passport valid for full stay; Israel stamps rejected

records.content: All short-stay visitors must register with police within one week of arrival; failure results in fines on departure. This is typically handled by the host company or travel agency.
records.title: Police registration required within one week

records.content: A visa is mandatory, obtained via the Libyan Embassy in London. A Libyan visa issued overseas may not be recognised in some areas or at certain ports of entry due to the current political situation.
records.notes: Fast-changing given the fragmented political/security situation — review at least quarterly.
records.title: Visa mandatory; overseas-issued visas may not be recognised everywhere

records.content: Healthcare is substandard compared to UK facilities, with acute shortages of skilled personnel and medical supplies, particularly for chronic conditions such as diabetes. Private clinics exist in Tripoli, but medical evacuation to Malta or Europe may be necessary for serious conditions.
records.title: Substandard; evacuation to Malta/Europe often needed

records.content: Key health risks include leishmaniasis, West Nile virus, and schistosomiasis.
records.title: Leishmaniasis, West Nile virus, schistosomiasis

records.content: Avoid border regions with Mali, Niger and Algeria (extremist group activity) and the coastal road between Zawiyah and Tripoli (very high carjacking/robbery risk). Southern Fezzan Province has the highest terrorist concentration.
records.title: Avoid border regions and the Zawiyah-Tripoli coastal road

records.content: The political situation is fragile and the security situation remains dangerous and unpredictable. A UN-facilitated ceasefire is in place between eastern and western armed forces, but localised armed group violence persists: significant armed clashes broke out across Tripoli on 12 May, and a ceasefire agreed on 14 May has largely held. Earlier Tripoli clashes killed 32 people and injured over 150 in 2022, and in August 2023 fighting in central Tripoli caused roadblocks and the temporary closure of Mitiga Airport.
records.notes: Fast-changing — review at least monthly. The FCDO extract reviewed on 2026-09-21 did not state the year of the 12 May clashes (the previous version of this record said May 2024) — confirm on the FCDO page.
records.title: Fragile political situation; localised armed clashes persist

records.content: Terrorist groups in Libya have intent to carry out kidnappings targeting foreign nationals; criminal gangs also kidnap and may sell hostages to terrorist groups. Oil and gas workers are highly likely to be viewed as high-value targets, and British nationals are considered high-value hostages.
records.notes: Fast-changing — review at least monthly. Directly relevant to any oil & gas personnel travel to Libya.
records.title: Oil and gas workers viewed as high-value targets

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Libya and against all but essential travel to other parts.
records.title: FCDO advises against all/all but essential travel to parts of Libya

records.content: Terrorist attacks in Libya cannot be ruled out and may target locations frequented by foreigners. Daesh and AQIM operate primarily in the Fezzan Province (south) but can move to other areas. Recent attacks include a 2022 car bombing near a military camp.
records.title: High terrorism threat; Daesh/AQIM active in Fezzan

records.content: 911 covers ambulance, fire and police services nationally. Mexico City Tourist Police: (0052) 55 5207 4155.
records.title: Single emergency number: 911 (ambulance, fire, police)

records.content: Quintana Roo state charges an entry tax (payable online or at the airport). A departure tax may apply when leaving by air or land depending on location.
records.title: Quintana Roo entry tax and possible departure tax

records.content: Passport must be valid for the duration of stay; the Mexican Embassy recommends at least 180 days' validity (the maximum tourist stay length). Onward transit through other countries may require 6 months' validity.
records.title: Passport valid for stay; 180 days recommended

records.content: No visa is needed for tourist visits by British citizens; a passport stamp indicates the allowed stay. Entry by land requires completion of an online immigration form via the INM website beforehand. Work or study requires a visa arranged before travel.
records.title: No visa needed for tourism; land entrants must file online form

records.content: Outside state capitals and larger urban areas, medical and emergency services may be limited. Many hospitals do not work directly with insurance and require upfront payment.
records.title: Limited outside major cities; upfront payment often required

records.content: Health risks include Zika virus, chikungunya, dengue, and air pollution; altitude sickness is a risk in certain regions.
records.title: Zika, chikungunya, dengue and air pollution

records.content: Only boiled or bottled water should be consumed and ice in drinks avoided, to prevent waterborne illness including Cyclospora.
records.title: Boiled/bottled water recommended

records.content: The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to the city of Acapulco due to infrastructure damage from Hurricane Otis (2023) and unpredictable security.
records.title: Acapulco: all but essential travel advised against

records.content: Drug-related violence has escalated, including gang-related shootings in tourist zones such as Cancun. Express kidnappings (forcing victims to withdraw ATM funds) occur in urban areas; longer-term kidnappings also happen. Impersonators posing as police demand bribes.
records.title: Drug-related violence and express kidnapping risk

records.content: Driving standards differ significantly from UK norms with potholes and unpredictable conditions; many drivers lack insurance. Avoid isolated roads and use toll roads where possible; vehicle hijackings reported along the Pacific Highway.
records.title: Poor conditions; avoid isolated roads, use toll roads

records.content: There is a high threat of terrorist attack globally affecting UK interests and British nationals; attacks in Mexico cannot be ruled out.
records.title: Terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out

records.content: General emergency number: 112.
records.notes: No dedicated national ambulance service — see Health category.
records.title: General emergency number: 112

records.content: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date.
records.title: Passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond arrival

records.content: A visa is mandatory and must be obtained before departure via the online Nigerian Immigration Services portal; visa on arrival is no longer available. Valid CERPAC/Green Card residence-permit holders are exempt.
records.title: Visa required in advance — visa on arrival no longer available

records.content: A yellow fever vaccination certificate is required (exemptions for infants under 8 months and adults 61+), plus an online Nigeria Health Declaration Form before entry (including transit passengers). Additional Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) disease screening protocols have been announced and may be implemented at border entry points, including enhanced monitoring of air passengers arriving from East and Central Africa.
records.title: Yellow fever certificate, health declaration and Ebola (Bundibugyo) screening

records.content: There is no national ambulance service and hospital ambulances are severely restricted; you may need to arrange local transport. General emergency number: 112.
records.title: No national ambulance service

records.content: Medical standards differ significantly from the UK. Public hospitals require payment and private facilities are considerably more expensive, with possible overcrowding and equipment shortages.
records.title: Standards vary; public hospitals require payment upfront

records.content: High levels of violent street crime include armed robbery and carjackings, with British nationals sometimes targeted as perceived wealthy. Criminal groups run illegal checkpoints on major highways, notably the Abuja-Kaduna route.
records.title: High levels of armed robbery and carjacking; illegal checkpoints

records.content: Kidnappings are widespread and could occur anywhere in Nigeria, affecting foreign nationals, aid workers and tourists. Criminal kidnap is particularly severe in the northwest (Zamfara, Katsina, Kaduna) and central states.
records.title: Kidnapping widespread and could occur anywhere

records.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Nigeria. The primary threat is from ISWA and Boko Haram, based mainly in Borno, Yobe and Adamawa states, though attacks have occurred more widely. Targets include places of worship, markets, hotels and public gatherings.
records.title: Very likely terrorism risk, concentrated in the northeast

records.content: Dial 113 for an ambulance.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 113

records.content: Your passport must have been issued less than 10 years before your arrival date, and have an expiry date at least 3 months after you plan to leave the Schengen area.
records.title: Passport must meet Schengen age/validity rules

records.content: British citizens can enter visa-free for tourism, family visits or short study for up to 90 days in any 180-day period, calculated across the whole Schengen area. Overstaying risks a Schengen ban of up to 3 years.
records.title: Visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period

records.content: UK nationals can access state-provided hospital treatment using their passport, though some doctors may charge separately. A GHIC or EHIC card is not an alternative to full travel insurance.
