records.title: State hospital treatment accessible with passport; GHIC/EHIC not a substitute for insurance

records.content: Nearly half of Norway lies within the Arctic Circle. In these extremely isolated regions, emergency medical assistance and search and rescue are limited, and winter temperatures can fall to -25°C and below with severe wind chill.
records.notes: Relevant for any North Sea / Arctic oil & gas site travel.
records.title: Arctic areas have limited emergency response

records.content: Avalanche season extends well into April, with associated flood and landslide risk in mountainous and exposed areas; weather can shift rapidly even in summer at high elevations.
records.title: Avalanche, flood and landslide risk into spring

records.content: Terrorist attacks in Norway cannot be ruled out, in line with a global high threat level affecting UK interests and nationals.
records.title: Terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out

records.content: Call 9999 and ask for an ambulance.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 9999

records.content: British-Omani dual nationals should note Oman does not recognise dual citizenship; authorities may confiscate one passport.
records.title: Oman does not recognise dual citizenship

records.content: Your passport must remain valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date in Oman.
records.title: Passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond arrival

records.content: British citizens can enter visa-free for stays up to 14 days. Longer stays or non-tourism purposes need an advance e-visa (apply online rather than on arrival to reduce rejection risk). Overstay penalties run up to 10 OMR/day, max 500 OMR, plus possible detention.
records.title: Visa-free for 14 days; e-visa recommended for longer stays

records.content: Healthcare facilities are comparable to UK standards, but British nationals must use the private healthcare system. Travellers without adequate insurance or funds may be prevented from leaving Oman until bills are settled.
records.title: Good standard but private-only for British nationals

records.content: Road accident rates are significantly higher than UK standards, with wandering livestock and flash-flood-prone wadis outside Muscat. Desert travel requires well-equipped vehicles and, where possible, convoy travel.
records.title: Higher accident rates; hazards outside Muscat

records.content: Oman enforces strict Islamic law: public alcohol consumption or being intoxicated at airports, e-cigarettes/vapes (banned outright), unmarried cohabitation, and same-sex relations are all illegal, with drug possession carrying severe penalties including potential death sentence.
records.title: Strict Islamic law — alcohol, vaping, cohabitation, same-sex relations

records.content: Terrorist attacks in Oman cannot be ruled out and could target residential compounds, military, oil, transport and aviation interests, as well as restaurants and hotels. In July 2024 six people died in a shooting near a mosque in the Wadi Kabir area of Muscat.
records.title: Terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out

records.content: Products made from wild animal skins, archaeological artefacts without authorisation, and wildlife-derived crafts (e.g. condor feathers, turtle shells) are prohibited on export/import; coca leaves cannot be exported to the UK.
records.title: Wildlife/artefact export restrictions; coca leaves barred from UK

records.content: Passport should have an expiry date at least 6 months after arrival. British citizens can travel visa-free for tourism, typically granted up to 90 days in a 180-day period on arrival, extendable by immigration officials to a maximum of 183 days within 365 days. A passport stamp is required for land entry/exit. One laptop and 2 mobile phones can be brought in tax-free.
records.title: Visa-free up to 90 days (extendable); land entry requires a stamp

records.content: General emergency ambulance number: 106. Lima private emergency services: Alerta Med +51 1 416 6767, Clave Médica +51 1 467 4861.
records.title: Ambulance: 106 (general); private services in Lima

records.content: Medical treatment is not easily available and can be more difficult to access outside Lima. Many medications are available over the counter but some require a local prescription.
records.title: Healthcare

records.content: Peru is experiencing a major dengue outbreak following floods; other risks include Oropouche virus disease, yellow fever, malaria and Zika. Altitude sickness poses a serious risk in Cusco, Puno, the Colca Canyon and Kuelap.
records.title: Disease risks

records.content: Mugging and theft are significant in Lima, Cusco and Arequipa. 'Express kidnapping' targets tourists via fake taxi drivers who force ATM withdrawals, including risks at Jorge Chávez Airport and bus terminals. Even small amounts of methanol in counterfeit alcohol can kill.
records.title: Crime

records.content: The FCDO advises against all but essential travel to parts of Peru, including border areas with Ecuador, Colombia and Brazil, and the VRAEM (Valley of the Apurímac, Ene and Mantaro rivers), where remnants of the Shining Path guerrilla group remain active in coca-growing areas.
records.title: Advice level

records.content: Demonstrations are unpredictable and can escalate quickly, causing roadblocks, travel disruption (including trains) and suspension of immigration services at land borders. Foreign nationals participating in political activity risk detention or deportation. Recent protests have occurred in Lima's historic centre and in Arequipa, Cusco and Puno.
records.title: Protests

records.content: Emergency medical number: 999.
records.title: Emergency medical number: 999

records.content: As a visitor, your passport must be valid for at least 6 months from the date you arrive.
records.title: Passport must be valid at least 6 months for visitors

records.content: Transit passengers face strict drug policy — even residual/trace amounts can lead to arrest — and transit stays cannot exceed 24 hours.
records.title: Transit passengers face strict drug policy, 24-hour limit

records.content: Full British citizen passport holders can get a tourist visa on arrival; other passport types or non-tourism purposes need to apply in advance. Stays over 30 days require an extension via the Ministry of Interior before expiry.
records.title: Tourist visa on arrival for full British citizen passport holders

records.content: Healthcare facilities are similar to the UK, but visitors must pay for treatment — comprehensive travel health insurance with adequate coverage is essential.
records.title: Similar standard to the UK but payment required

records.content: Public drinking can mean up to 6 months' imprisonment; unmarried cohabitation, sex outside marriage and same-sex relations are illegal; drug possession has zero tolerance; photographing people without consent can mean imprisonment or fines up to 100,000 QAR; e-cigarettes are criminalised.
records.title: Severe penalties for alcohol, relationships, drugs, vaping, photography

records.content: Terrorist attacks in Qatar cannot be ruled out, with threats specifically mentioning Western interests including hotels, restaurants and shopping centres.
records.title: Attacks cannot be ruled out; Western-linked venues flagged

records.content: Dial 112 and ask for an ambulance.
records.title: Emergency number: 112

records.content: A visa is required before travel, applied for in person at a visa application centre (London, Manchester or Edinburgh) to provide biometric data. This is only relevant to travellers who choose to go against FCDO advice.
records.notes: The FCDO advises against all travel — see the SECURITY category.
records.title: Visa required in advance despite FCDO advising against all travel

records.content: Medical care in Russia may not meet Western standards. Hospitals may request payment before treatment, and in remote regions may not use disposable IV supplies/syringes/needles as standard practice.
records.title: May not meet Western standards; bring own medical supplies in remote areas

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to Russia. This reflects the ongoing war with Ukraine (drone attacks and explosions near the border and in major cities), heightened terrorism risk, and a legal environment in which foreigners can face lengthy imprisonment on limited grounds, with extremely limited UK consular ability to assist. Airspace closures during drone attacks have caused frequent and unpredictable flight delays, diversions and cancellations.
records.notes: Fast-changing — review at least monthly given the conflict.
records.title: FCDO advises against all travel to Russia

records.content: Since December 2024 Russia has expanded liability for foreigners suspected of acting against Russian interests (e.g. displaying LGBT+ symbols, expressing support for Ukraine online). Dual British-Russian nationals are especially vulnerable, as Russian authorities may deny UK consular access to detainees.
records.title: Expanded legal risk for foreigners, especially dual nationals

records.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Russia — the March 2024 Crocus City Hall attack near Moscow killed 145 people. Large gatherings, concerts and popular tourist sites are considered at risk.
records.title: Terrorists very likely to try to carry out attacks

records.content: Saudi Red Crescent Authority ambulance emergency number: 997.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 997

records.content: Civil defence and fire emergency number: 998.
records.title: Civil defence / fire emergency number: 998

records.content: National police emergency number: 911.
records.notes: Cross-check locally; numbering has changed in some regions in recent years.
records.title: Police emergency number: 911

records.content: Traffic police emergency number: 993.
records.title: Traffic police number: 993

records.content: You may not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia if your passport shows that you have travelled to, or were born in, Israel.
records.title: Entry may be refused for prior travel to, or birth in, Israel

records.content: Your passport must remain valid for at least 6 months beyond your arrival date in Saudi Arabia. You will not be permitted entry if your passport has been reported lost or stolen.
records.notes: Stated for British nationals; verify equivalent rule for other nationalities.
records.title: Passport must be valid at least 6 months beyond arrival

records.content: A transit visa is required if you will pass through Saudi immigration, are travelling on separate tickets, or have a layover exceeding 12 hours. Overland travellers via the Bahrain causeway should verify their visa permits that route.
records.title: Transit visa needed for some layovers

records.content: A visa is required. Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA): tourism, business, study, medical treatment or Umrah outside Hajj season; valid 730 days, multiple entries, 180 days total, no health insurance included. E-Visa: tourists only; valid 365 days, multiple entries, 90 days total, includes health insurance cover up to 100,000 SAR. Electronic Visa Waiver: tourism, business, medical treatment, study or Umrah; single entry, up to 180 days, apply 48 hours to 90 days before travel, no health insurance included.
records.notes: Stated for British nationals — requirements vary by nationality.
records.title: Visa required — three route options depending on purpose

records.content: Heat stroke and dehydration are a real risk during the summer months. Contagious diseases can spread rapidly, particularly during Hajj and Ramadan when very large crowds gather.
records.title: Heat, dehydration and contagious disease risk

records.content: Some UK prescription and over-the-counter medicines are controlled substances in Saudi Arabia. If you need to bring medication, carry official documentation from your doctor stating the amount prescribed and drug/dosage details. A UK prescription is not valid locally — only a Saudi-licensed doctor can issue a prescription there.
records.title: Some UK medicines are controlled substances in Saudi Arabia

records.content: Healthcare facilities in major Saudi cities are of a high standard. Most towns have health centres or basic hospitals, though serious cases may require transfer to a major city.
records.title: High-standard healthcare in major cities

records.content: Check the latest vaccine recommendations for Saudi Arabia at least 8 weeks before travel via TravelHealthPro or the NHS travel vaccinations service. Proof of yellow fever vaccination is required if arriving from an endemic area, and the meningococcal quadrivalent vaccine is required for Hajj/Umrah pilgrims.
records.title: Check current vaccine recommendations before travel

records.content: Avoid the vicinity of security and military facilities, which have been targeted in the past. Travel insurance may be invalidated if you travel against FCDO advice, so check your policy against the current advice before travelling.
records.title: Stay away from security and military facilities

records.content: Since 13 July the Houthis (a military group in Yemen) have launched missiles and drones at cities, airports, military and energy sites across Saudi Arabia, including Abha, Jizan, Najran, Riyadh, Jeddah and Yanbu, as well as at shipping in the Red Sea. Iranian strikes have also occurred since 8 July, and unforeseen escalation in the region is possible. Expect possible flight cancellations and airspace closures, and take care around transport infrastructure such as airports and ports. (FCDO Saudi Arabia page shown as updated 20 September 2026.)
records.title: Active Houthi missile/drone attacks on Saudi Arabia and Iranian strikes; regional escalation risk

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel within 10km of the Saudi–Yemen border, and against all but essential travel between 10–80km of it (including Abha and Khamis Mushait in Aseer province), due to the ongoing regional conflict.
records.title: Avoid all travel within 10km of the Yemen border

records.content: Passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date of arrival.
records.title: Passport valid at least 6 months after arrival

records.content: British citizens may enter visa-free for up to 3 months, but must show evidence of return or onward travel and proof of arranged accommodation. Stays beyond 3 months require registration with local authorities and a Carte d'étranger.
records.title: Visa

records.content: A yellow fever certificate is mandatory if arriving from a country with transmission risk, including transit through such a country (infants 9 months and under are exempt). Onward travel from Senegal to other countries may require a further yellow fever certificate given Senegal's own transmission risk.
records.title: Yellow fever

records.content: Ambulance emergency number: 15 (call and ask for an ambulance).
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 15

records.content: Medical facilities in Dakar are reasonable but limited elsewhere in Senegal. Health risks include dengue, Zika, yellow fever, Rift Valley fever and malaria; adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds for treatment and repatriation are essential.
records.title: Healthcare

records.content: Street crime is increasing in Dakar, including robbery and assault, hotel robberies at gunpoint, pickpocketing/bag-snatching, bogus taxi drivers at the airport and fake currency in cash exchanges.
records.title: Crime

records.content: Severe penalties apply for drug possession, use or trafficking (maximum trafficking sentence 20 years). Same-sex sexual acts are illegal and enforced; a March 2026 amendment increased sentences for same-sex relations to 5-10 years and criminalised the 'promotion, support or funding' of homosexuality, bisexuality and transsexuality.
records.title: Laws

records.content: Frequent demonstrations about political issues occur in Dakar and other cities and can turn violent; protestors have blocked roads, including airport routes. Foreign nationals have faced prosecution for attending unapproved protests.
records.title: Political unrest

records.content: Terrorist attacks in Senegal cannot be ruled out and could be indiscriminate, including in places visited by foreign nationals. JNIM operates in neighbouring Mali and has increasingly conducted attacks in southern and western Mali near the Senegalese border; remote regions and border areas also carry a kidnap risk.
records.title: Terrorism

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to Syria, making the published entry requirements largely theoretical; rules should be verified directly with Syrian authorities given the ongoing political transition.
records.title: FCDO advises against all travel to Syria

records.content: A visa is mandatory, applied for online, typically taking approximately 5-7 days to process though this can vary; passports must be valid for at least 3 months after the date of arrival. Israeli and Iranian citizens cannot enter, and travellers with Israeli stamps in their passport may be refused entry.
records.title: Visa mandatory; entry barred for Israeli/Iranian citizens

records.content: There is a very high threat of kidnapping from terrorists throughout Syria, including Al-Qaeda-affiliated groups and Daesh. British nationals are explicitly targeted and some hostages have been killed.
records.title: Very high kidnap threat; British nationals targeted

records.content: Landmines and other unexploded ordnance remain from the Syrian conflict, with particular risk in less populated and rural areas and near former conflict lines.
records.title: Landmine and unexploded ordnance risk

records.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Syria. Daesh continues to carry out regular attacks nationwide, including in Damascus — recent incidents include an explosives attack on the Four Seasons hotel and Tourism Ministry (7 July 2026, 1 killed, 36 injured), a café bombing in central Damascus (2 July 2026, 9 killed, 22 injured), and an attack on a Greek Orthodox church (2 June 2025, at least 30 killed).
records.title: Regular Daesh attacks nationwide, including Damascus

records.content: The security situation remains volatile following the fall of the Assad government; fighting and violence may occur around the country. Some areas, particularly Suwayda province, are controlled by local armed groups rather than the Syrian government.
records.title: Volatile situation post-Assad; some areas outside government control

records.content: Ambulance: 03 from landline, 003 from mobile. Fire: 01 landline / 001 mobile. Police: 02 landline / 002 mobile.
records.title: Ambulance: 03 (landline) / 003 (mobile)

records.content: Turkmenistan operates primarily on cash (manat); USD and EUR exchange easily at official rates but bring clean, new bills. ATMs in Ashgabat charge 3% per withdrawal. Manat cannot be reconverted to foreign currency, and export of manat is restricted.
records.notes: Operationally significant for any personnel travel — arrange cash logistics before travel.
records.title: Cash-based economy; manat cannot be reconverted

records.content: Passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the planned departure date from Turkmenistan.
records.title: Passport valid 6 months beyond planned departure

records.content: Registration is required if staying over 3 working days, typically handled by hotels or sponsors. A migration fee ($14 USD) and daily tourism tax ($2 USD) apply.
records.title: Registration required for stays over 3 working days

records.content: All visitors need a visa and a letter of invitation obtained beforehand (via a travel agent for tourism, or a company/ministry letter for business). Embassy applications take up to one month; visas on arrival are available at Ashgabat International Airport and select land borders. Transit visas (under 5 days) cannot be converted to tourist visas.
records.title: Visa mandatory; letter of invitation required

records.content: The quality of medical care is poor and considerably more expensive than in the UK. Basic or emergency services outside the capital are best avoided. There is no reciprocal healthcare agreement with the UK.
records.title: Poor quality and expensive; no reciprocal agreement

records.content: Typhoid and hepatitis A are endemic. Summer temperatures regularly exceed 45°C, requiring hydration and sun protection. Air quality in cities fluctuates periodically.
records.notes: Extreme summer heat directly relevant to any outdoor gas-field work.
records.title: Typhoid, hepatitis A, extreme summer heat

records.content: Drink or use only boiled and filtered or bottled water and avoid ice in drinks.
records.title: Only boiled/filtered or bottled water recommended

records.content: Driving conditions are hazardous outside urban areas, particularly at night, due to poor road conditions. Ashgabat enforces a 60 km/h speed limit via unmarked cameras. Use only licensed (white/green marked) taxis.
records.title: Hazardous outside urban areas at night

records.content: VPNs are illegal and blocked. Negative political commentary on social media is treated as an offence. Alcohol consumption in public spaces carries 100-manat fines; drug possession results in lengthy prison sentences under basic conditions. Male same-sex activity is criminalised.
records.title: VPNs illegal; strict alcohol and speech rules

records.content: Border areas near Afghanistan and Iran are tightly restricted with occasional unannounced closures. Photography of airports, military sites, police stations, government buildings and embassies is prohibited without permission.
records.notes: Relevant for any gas-field travel near restricted border zones.
records.title: Border areas restricted; photography of official sites banned

records.content: Although there is no recent history of terrorism in Turkmenistan, attacks cannot be ruled out given the broader global terrorism threat affecting British interests.
records.title: No recent history but attacks cannot be ruled out

records.content: Foreign currency must be declared on arrival or it may be confiscated. Tunisian dinars cannot be taken out of Tunisia — keep official exchange receipts. Drones are illegal without prior authorisation and will be confiscated; some smart devices (e.g. AI smart glasses, walkie-talkies) may also be restricted.
records.title: Dinars cannot be exported; drones need authorisation

records.content: Passport must be valid for the duration of the stay (damaged/torn passports can create exit difficulties). British citizens may visit without a visa for up to 90 days; ensure the passport is stamped on entry. Overstaying incurs fines payable at departure or in advance at police stations. Border officials may request contact details, travel tickets and accommodation proof.
records.title: Visa-free for up to 90 days; passport must be stamped

records.content: Ambulance emergency number: 190.
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 190

records.content: There is no provision of free medical attention for foreign nationals in Tunisia; medical expenses must be paid on the spot, sometimes before treatment, and costs can be high. Adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds are essential.
records.title: Healthcare

records.content: Possession of illegal drugs can lead to lengthy prison sentences and heavy fines. Same-sex sexual activity is illegal. Do not photograph government buildings or military sites. The drink-drive limit is stricter than in England and Wales.
records.title: Laws

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Tunisia (see the regional risks section for specifics, including border areas).
records.title: Advice level

records.content: Demonstrations occur occasionally, may start with little or no warning, tend to happen at weekends, and can turn violent; labour strikes may disrupt transport and border crossings.
records.title: Protests

records.content: Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Tunisia, with elevated risk at religious sites, tourist sites and festivals, public transport networks and areas where foreign nationals and tourists gather.
records.title: Terrorism

records.content: Passport must have an expiry date at least 6 months after the date of arrival.
records.title: Passport valid at least 6 months after arrival

records.content: A visa is required, applied for online via visas.immigration.go.ug; an authorisation letter with barcode is emailed and presented on arrival for the visa to be issued. Alternatively, an East African tourist visa (100 US dollars) allows multiple entries to Kenya, Rwanda and Uganda within 90 days. A yellow fever vaccination certificate must be carried and may be checked. Uganda closed its border with the DRC on 27 May (Ebola-related), with exceptions for authorised responders and humanitarian personnel.
records.title: Visa

records.content: Ambulance emergency number: 999 (call and ask for an ambulance).
records.title: Ambulance emergency number: 999

records.content: Medical facilities are limited, especially outside Kampala, and tourist areas may lack adequate care; serious illness or accidents may require air ambulance evacuation. Medical help at accident scenes is likely to be limited, particularly outside Kampala.
records.title: Healthcare

records.content: On 27 August 2026 the WHO declared the Uganda Ebola outbreak over, though risk of transmission from the DRC remains. Other risks include malaria, yellow fever, mpox and Marburg virus disease; around 1,400,000 adults aged 15+ in Uganda live with HIV.
records.title: Disease risks

records.content: Criminal kidnaps and targeted armed assaults are unlikely to be directed at tourists, but pickpocketing, mugging, vehicle theft from stopped traffic, boda-boda (motorbike taxi) muggings, and food/drink spiking (including methanol poisoning in alcoholic drinks) all occur.
records.title: Crime

records.content: Drug possession carries a maximum sentence of 20 years and trafficking life imprisonment. Uganda's Anti-Homosexuality Act 2023 imposes life imprisonment for same-sex sexual activity and up to the death penalty for 'aggravated' offences; 'promoting or supporting homosexuality' carries up to 20 years. Photographing military, diplomatic or official sites, and wearing camouflage/military-style clothing, are both illegal (the latter carrying a maximum sentence of life imprisonment).
records.title: Laws

records.content: Presidential and parliamentary elections were held on 15 January 2026, with inauguration on 12 May 2026. Elections and political events have led to protests and violence, including fatalities; police have used tear gas, rubber bullets and live ammunition against demonstrators, who should be avoided.
records.title: Political unrest

records.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Uganda, with potential targets including hotels, diplomatic sites, transport hubs, restaurants, places of worship, shopping centres and national parks. Recent incidents include attacks in December 2023, an October 2023 attack in Queen Elizabeth National Park killing two tourists and their driver, and a June 2023 attack killing 42 at a school in Mpondwe.
records.title: Terrorism

records.content: Dial 911 and ask for an ambulance.
records.title: Emergency number: 911

records.content: Travellers need either an approved ESTA (Visa Waiver Program) or a US visa before arrival — a valid ESTA/visa does not guarantee entry. You cannot use ESTA if you have prior arrests/convictions, were previously deported or refused entry, overstayed a past ESTA, or have travelled to Iran, Iraq, Libya, North Korea, Somalia, Sudan, Syria or Yemen since March 2011, or Cuba since 12 Jan 2021.
records.notes: Relevant for oil & gas travellers with Middle East travel history — check ESTA eligibility carefully.
records.title: ESTA or visa required before travel; ineligibility triggers

records.content: Your passport must be valid for the length of your planned stay in the US; many transit countries separately require 6 months' remaining validity.
records.title: Passport must be valid for the length of stay

records.content: Medical treatment is expensive and there are no special arrangements for British visitors; some hospitals require deposits from non-residents. Comprehensive travel health insurance is essential.
records.title: Medical treatment is expensive with no special arrangements for visitors

records.content: Crime linked to illegal drugs is significant in Mexican border areas of Arizona, California, New Mexico and Texas, though foreign nationals are not specifically targeted.
records.title: Drug-related crime near the Mexican border

records.content: Hurricane season runs June-November (Atlantic) and May-November (Pacific). Wildfires are prevalent in dry areas; earthquake risk is higher in Alaska, California, Hawaii, Oregon, Washington and Puerto Rico; tornadoes and flash floods can occur with minimal warning.
records.title: Hurricanes, wildfires, tornadoes and earthquakes by region

records.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in the US, with potential targets including crowded venues, transport hubs, sporting events and religious sites.
records.title: Terrorists very likely to try to carry out attacks

records.content: 911 covers ambulance, fire and police services.
records.title: Single emergency number: 911 (ambulance, fire, police)

records.content: Goods worth over $1,000 USD and cash/traveller's cheques of $10,000 USD or more must be declared on entry; import tax applies to new-looking items.
records.title: Declare goods over $1,000 and cash over $10,000

records.content: Venezuelan dual nationals must use Venezuelan identity documents for entry and exit; departure may be denied without a valid Venezuelan passport.
records.title: Venezuelan dual nationals must use Venezuelan documents

records.content: Passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond the planned departure date. Entry is denied if the document is reported lost or stolen.
records.title: Passport valid 6 months beyond departure

records.content: Arrival by air allows a stay of up to 90 days visa-free on a tourist card issued on arrival, with a return/onward ticket required. Arrival overland or by sea may require an advance visa. Tourist cards can be extended up to 90 more days via SAIME. Work, NGO, journalism or study activities require an advance visa.
records.title: Visa-free tourist card for up to 90 days by air

records.content: The Venezuelan Pharmaceutical Federation has reported an 80% shortage of medical supplies due to the economic crisis. Travellers must bring sufficient medication for their entire stay, plus extra in case of delayed return.
records.title: Severe medicine shortages — bring a full supply plus extra

records.content: Private clinics in major cities offer acceptable care for routine treatment but face acute shortages of medical supplies and medicines. Public facilities are poor with chronic shortages. Comprehensive treatment may require medical evacuation.
records.title: Public facilities poor; medicine shortages acute

records.content: Health risks include yellow fever, dengue fever, schistosomiasis, and altitude sickness (particularly in Mérida, Táchira and Trujillo states).
records.title: Yellow fever, dengue, schistosomiasis

records.content: Armed robbery, mugging, carjacking and burglary are prevalent and often violent. Use only pre-booked taxis from reputable companies; do not resist an attacker. High-risk areas include Zulia, Táchira, Apure states, and the Orinoco Mining Arc.
records.notes: Zulia state borders Lake Maracaibo's oil operations — directly relevant to any oil & gas travel.
records.title: Armed robbery and carjacking prevalent and often violent

records.content: Some foreign nationals, including Europeans, have been detained and accused of terrorism. Support from the FCDO to detained British nationals may be severely limited.
records.title: Foreign nationals detained and accused of terrorism

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to parts of Venezuela and against all but essential travel to other parts.
records.notes: Fast-changing — review at least monthly given the unstable political situation.
records.title: FCDO advises against all/essential travel to parts of Venezuela

records.content: The UK does not recognise the current Venezuelan administration. Military presence is visible in major cities and consular access/support to British nationals may be severely limited. A 'state of external commotion' was declared on 3 January due to airstrikes.
records.title: UK does not recognise current administration; consular support limited

records.content: The FCDO advises against all travel to Yemen; the published entry requirements apply only to those who choose to travel against that advice.
records.title: FCDO advises against all travel to Yemen

records.content: A visa is required and must be obtained from the Yemeni Embassy in the UK before travel — there is no visa on arrival. Passports must be valid for at least 6 months after the date of arrival. Stays of more than two weeks require registration with Yemen's immigration authorities after arrival.
records.title: Visa required in advance; no visa on arrival

records.content: A de facto ceasefire between the Houthis and the Yemeni government has held since April 2022, formalised by a UN-announced commitment on 23 December 2023, but sporadic incidents continue along frontlines and the security situation remains volatile; large-scale conflict could resume without warning.
records.title: De facto ceasefire holding but volatile since Apr 2022

records.content: Travel to Houthi-controlled areas is strongly advised against. Red Sea shipping faces an ongoing risk from Houthi forces due to the potential for misidentification.
records.title: Avoid Houthi-controlled areas; Red Sea shipping risk

records.content: There is a very high and constant threat of kidnap across Yemen. AQAP has called for continued kidnapping of Westerners, and criminal groups may sell hostages to terrorist organisations.
records.title: Very high, constant kidnap threat

records.content: Landmines from the current and previous conflicts are a risk on Yemen's roads.
records.title: Landmine risk on roads

records.content: Terrorists are very likely to try to carry out attacks in Yemen. Al-Qaida in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP) and Islamic State-Yemen pose a heightened threat in Abyan, Marib, Hadramawt and Shabwah governorates, using bombings, assassinations and suicide attacks against hotels, airports, transport routes and government buildings.
records.title: Very likely terrorist attacks, heightened in four governorates

records.content: Hurricane Polo is affecting Mexico's southwestern Pacific coast. Heavy rain is expected to continue during the week of 21 September 2026 and may cause life-threatening flooding and landslides. FCDO advises monitoring updates from the US National Hurricane Center and the Mexican Meteorological Service and following local authority guidance; the system is forecast to reach Baja California around 26-27 September 2026.
records.notes: Fast-changing — active storm; review frequently and remove/update once the system has passed. See also Current Intelligence event nhc-hurricane-polo-mx-2026-09-21 for real-time NHC advisory detail.
records.title: Hurricane Polo: heavy rain, flooding and landslide risk (Guerrero/Michoacan/Oaxaca)

records.content: The Ecuadorean government declared a 60-day state of emergency from 15 September 2026 for security reasons in 8 provinces (Guayas, Manabí, Santa Elena, Los Ríos, El Oro, Pichincha, Esmeraldas and Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas), with greater police and military presence on the streets. A curfew (00:00-05:00) applies in El Oro, Guayas, Los Ríos and Manabí from 17 to 30 September 2026.
records.notes: New record — first TI baseline coverage for Ecuador, reflecting a genuinely current, FCDO-sourced security situation rather than a historical backfill.
records.title: 60-day state of emergency declared 15 Sep 2026 (8 provinces)

records.content: FCDO advises against all but essential travel to the Coastal Region provinces of Esmeraldas, Manabí, Santa Elena, Guayas, El Oro, Los Ríos and Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas (airside transit at Guayaquil airport excepted), and to areas within 20km of the Ecuador-Colombia border (with specific exceptions in Carchi province).
records.notes: New record — first TI baseline coverage for Ecuador.
records.title: Advises against all but essential travel to coastal provinces and Colombia border zone

records.content: Santa Marta remains under heightened security measures following a major operation against armed groups in the area, with damage to vehicles and local businesses, disruption to transport services, and school/business closures; additional police and military deployment is expected. Risks are also present along Route 90 (Troncal del Caribe), the main transport corridor linking Santa Marta with Tayrona National Park, Palomino and Riohacha, used by domestic and international visitors.
records.notes: Fast-changing — review at least monthly while heightened measures remain in place.
records.title: Santa Marta: heightened security measures after operation against armed groups

records.content: To use a local Kazakhstani SIM card, you must verify your device's IMEI at the imei.kz portal. If you do not verify your device (or your stay exceeds 30 days without doing so), your local SIM card will be blocked after 30 days and you will not be able to activate another local SIM. Consider using a global eSIM instead if you would rather not complete IMEI verification.
records.notes: New record — not previously represented in TI's Kazakhstan coverage.
records.title: Local SIM cards require IMEI verification at imei.kz

Verified 22 Sep 2026 from ReliefWeb's own official documentation (apidoc.reliefweb.int, including its Swagger/OpenAPI spec) and its Terms of Service page. API v2, base https://api.reliefweb.int/v2, read-only, JSON responses; example endpoint https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=...&limit=2. Every call requires an 'appname' parameter, and per ReliefWeb's own documentation, 'From 1 November 2025, API users will require a pre-approved appname' obtained via a request form with roughly one business day's turnaround — TI does NOT currently hold a pre-approved appname, so automationPermission is recorded as UNKNOWN rather than PERMITTED (unlike GDACS, which explicitly permits anyone/any automated use with no onboarding). Quotas: max 1000 entries per call, max 1000 calls per day. Rights position is layered: the API's own Swagger spec states its metadata/schema is licensed CC0 (Creative Commons Zero – Public Domain); OCHA's general site footer states CC BY 4.0; but ReliefWeb's own Terms of Service explicitly warns that 'Reports, Jobs and Training data available via ReliefWeb API is contributed by information partners and may contain copyrighted material owned by the original source. You should respect the intellectual property rights of the original source.' contentRights is therefore recorded conservatively as FACTUAL_SUMMARY_ONLY — TI extracts only concise factual claims from ReliefWeb items, never reproduces original report text, regardless of the underlying licence of any individual report. ReliefWeb itself is a UN OCHA platform, but the great majority of its content is authored by information partners (UN agencies, NGOs, governments, and commercial analysis firms) rather than by OCHA directly — the originating organisation behind each individual report must be identified and used for independenceGroupId per-observation; ReliefWeb-as-platform is never itself treated as an independent corroborating source alongside its own contributors. A direct live test of the reports endpoint (https://api.reliefweb.int/v2/reports?appname=apidoc&limit=2) was blocked by bot detection in this session — genuinely unresolved; REQUIRES VERIFICATION for any future production integration, alongside the pre-approved-appname gap.
